hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's recent purchasing behaviour (spend, trip frequency, basket size over the last 4-16 weeks, days since last purchase) is a strong predictor of its next 4-week spend, far better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added rolling-window transaction aggregates (spend/trips/lines/qty/discounts at 28/56/84/112 days), days-since-last-purchase, basket stats, store count, and spend trend ratio.
reasoning_summary: Spend is highly autocorrelated; recent-window aggregates capture household activity level and momentum, which should dominate calendar/demographic features.

hypothesis: Where a household's recent dollars go (department-level spend mix and category shares over 28/112 days) predicts its 4-week future spend beyond overall spend/trip aggregates.
transformation_description: Added 28-day department spend totals and 112-day department spend shares (~95 dept features) on top of E001's rolling aggregates; parent E001.
reasoning_summary: Department mix captures what a household buys, not just how much — e.g. heavy grocery vs. drug-GM buyers should have different forward spend levels and trajectories, adding signal the pure volume aggregates miss.

hypothesis: The temporal shape of recent spend — weekly spend lags, trend, volatility, gaps between trips, and aligned 28-day periodic lags — predicts future 4-week spend beyond E002's window aggregates and department mix.
transformation_description: Added 35 temporal-structure features (weekly spend/trips lags w-1..w-8, 4/8/16-week sums, std, zero-week count, slope, top-week share, EWMA half-life 2 and 4, recent-vs-older ratios, aligned 28-day lags p1-p4 with diff/ratio, trip-gap mean/std/max/cv) on top of E002.
reasoning_summary: Spend is bursty and habitual; lagged weekly values and aligned 28-day lags capture autocorrelation at the exact forecast horizon, while volatility and gap regularity distinguish stable vs erratic spenders that averages miss.

hypothesis: Retailer marketing touchpoints — active/recent campaign targeting (TypeA/B/C), coupon redemptions, and display/mailer exposure of a household's recent purchases — predict future 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Standalone marketing-exposure feature set (15 features: campaign targeting counts by type and recency, coupon-redemption recency/count, display/mailer-exposed spend, share and line counts over the last 28 days) with no transaction-history or demographic features.
reasoning_summary: Marketing exposure correlates strongly with spend raw (r≈0.79 for display-exposed spend), and campaign targeting shows a small positive partial signal (r≈0.018) after controlling for recent spend; this tests whether the marketing channel carries standalone predictive signal before merging it into the E003 stack.

hypothesis: Beyond spend level and timing, HOW a household shops predicts its 4-week future spend: tenure-adjusted purchase intensity, acceleration vs lifetime rate, and 84-day basket structure (mean/max/std basket value, lines per trip, spend per line, product/store diversity, top-store concentration, weekend and morning trip shares).
transformation_description: Added 18 basket-composition and tenure features on top of E003's full table (temporal_structure.parquet merged with new basket/tenure block).
reasoning_summary: E003's temporal features captured when households spend; these features capture how they spend (basket size/variety/concentration and purchase acceleration), which should add independent signal about future demand.

hypothesis: Target-aligned lag structure and shopping mix predict future spend: spend in the exact same 28-day window 4–52 weeks ago (periodicity/seasonality incl. same-window-last-year), 4-week-scale burstiness (zero lagged windows), fine-grained recency (last 7/14 days), and private-brand/coupon/category concentration over 84 days add signal beyond E005's week-level lags.
transformation_description: On top of E005's full table: 11 target-aligned 28d lag windows (tlag_2..tlag_13), lag stats (mean/std/max/zero count, YoY and prev-window ratios), spend_7/spend_14/spend_7_over_28, private-brand share, coupon-discount share, top-commodity share, distinct commodities, and 84d coupon redemptions.
reasoning_summary: The target is a 28-day window, so aligning lag windows to the target window (rather than calendar weeks) should capture household-level seasonality and burstiness at the right scale; fine-grained recency and shopping-mix features capture churn and style-of-shopping effects that week-level lags miss.

hypothesis: Fine-grained weekly purchase history (last 26 weeks of per-week spend/trip/line counts, 4-week block lags, 52-week same-period sum, activity recency in weeks) adds predictive detail beyond the 28-day lag grid in E006.
transformation_description: Added 71 weekly-history features on top of E006's full table: per-week spend lags ws_1..ws_26, trip/line lags wt/wl_1..13, 4-week block sums wblk_1..6, 52-week same-period spend with ratio, 26-week mean/std/max/nonzero-count/slope, weeks-since-active, and 13-week trip/line means.
reasoning_summary: The target is a 4-week spend window, so per-week granularity and 4-week block lags align exactly with the prediction horizon; the 52-week same-period sum captures annual seasonality that 28-day lags miss.

hypothesis: Retailer marketing exposure (campaign targeting by type/recency, coupon redemptions, in-store display and mailer spend shares in the last 28 days) carries incremental signal about a household's next-4-week spend beyond its full behavioral history.
transformation_description: Merged E004's 13 as-of-consistent marketing-exposure features (campaign targeting counts by type and recency, coupon redemption recency/counts, display/mailer spend shares over 28d) onto E007's full 268-feature table.
reasoning_summary: E004 tested marketing features standalone (MAE 71.3) but they were never combined with the behavioral main line; display/mailer spend shares are genuinely new information not captured by transaction aggregates, so merging may add signal where standalone testing failed.

hypothesis: Recency-weighted spend (half-life EWMAs), longer purchase windows (91/182/364d), deeper target-aligned lags (14-18), weekly day-of-week/time-of-day rhythm, brand/dept diversity, and decay interactions carry signal about future 4-week spend beyond E008's fixed windows.
transformation_description: On top of E008's full table: added 88 features — EWMA weekly spend (half-life 2/4/8), 26-week spend stats, 91/182/364d spend/trip/line aggregates, tlag_14..18 + yoy ratio, day-of-week and time-of-day shares, private-brand share and dept diversity, recency-decay interactions, zero/low-spend flags, target-window seasonality, and log1p versions of key skewed features.
reasoning_summary: EWMAs emphasize recent behaviour more smoothly than fixed windows; long windows capture stable level and YoY seasonality; rhythm/diversity capture shopping style. Correlations confirm ewma_4 (0.77) and spend_91 (0.77) beat prior best features.

hypothesis: Product-level shopping habits predict future spend: repurchase loyalty (share of recent spend on commodities/products bought in the prior window), basket concentration (top-k commodity/manufacturer shares, entropy), breadth of basket (distinct commodities/products/manufacturers across 28/84/182d), fresh-vs-packaged and vice-category mix, brand loyalty, staple momentum, product stickiness, and newness of recent purchases.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full 371-feature table: added 35 product-habit features built by joining transactions to the products hierarchy — repeat-purchase rates (rep_com_28/56, rep_prod_28, rep_fresh_28), concentration (top1/5/10 commodity shares, top1/5 manufacturer shares), breadth & entropy (distinct commodities/products/manufacturers, entropy), fresh/alcohol/tobacco/gas/private-label/coupon-misc shares, brand loyalty, staple momentum, top-20-product stickiness, and new-commodity share.
reasoning_summary: Breadth and repetition of recent product-level purchases capture household shopping style and habit stability, which should refine spend forecasts beyond pure spend totals; breadth features alone correlate 0.7+ with the target.

hypothesis: The E009 table contains an accidental row-order 'index' column plus 16 columns that are constant or all-NaN in the training snapshots; these add noise rather than signal, so pruning them improves validation MAE.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full table: dropped 17 columns — the row-order 'index' artifact and 16 columns constant or all-NaN across train snapshots. No features added or removed otherwise.
reasoning_summary: The 'index' column is a pure row-order artifact (corr with target 0.04) and the dead columns carry no train information; removing them should reduce noise/overfitting and slightly improve validation MAE.

hypothesis: A simple, regularized 3-feature model — recent 28-day spend, the mean of target-aligned 28-day lag spends (tlag_2..tlag_15), and an EWMA of weekly spend — predicts 4-week future spend better than the 370-feature table when the model overfits noisy/high-cardinality features.
transformation_description: New table: household_key, snapshot_day + only 3 numeric features (spend_28, tlag_mean, ewma_4) copied from the E009 table.
reasoning_summary: E010/E011/E012 showed adding features no longer helps; a deliberately tiny, low-variance feature set may beat the full table if the fixed model overfits.

hypothesis: Beyond spend level and timing, store affinity (concentration/entropy of spend across stores), basket shape (stock-up vs top-up trips), lifetime weekly churn history (zero-week streaks), discount-type mix, and demographic×spend interactions predict 4-week future spend.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full 371-feature table: added 35 features — store-affinity shares/HHI/entropy (84d), basket-shape percentiles and stock-up shares, weekly zero-streak/churn stats, discount-type shares, and demographic ordinal × spend interactions.
reasoning_summary: Store loyalty and trip type capture spending capacity and regularity that raw spend aggregates miss; churn streaks and interactions let the model adapt spend-to-spend mapping to household type.

hypothesis: Robust distribution statistics of weekly spend (median/quartiles/IQR over 26 weeks, trips over 13 weeks), zero-streak and active-week counts, and spend-per-active-day capture the household's typical (not just mean) spend level and activity regularity, which predict 4-week future spend better than E009's mean-based features.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full 371-feature table: added 44 features from three saved candidate sets — robust weekly/trip statistics (rb_wmed26, rb_wq25/75, rb_wiqr, rb_tmed13, rb_tq25/75, rb_tcv13, rb_max28...), active-week counts and spend-per-active-day, store-affinity/zero-streak/big-trip features from E013's new set.
reasoning_summary: The new robust statistics correlate strongly with the target (rb_wq75 r=0.79, rb_wmed26 r=0.74) and are not in E009; adding them gives the model the household's typical spend level rather than only recent means, which should reduce MAE.

hypothesis: Household-level persistent effects — stable traits like loyalty, size, income and shopping style that are constant per household but not captured by any aggregate feature — predict future 4-week spend. Since every validation household also appears in ~12 earlier train rows, giving the model household_key as a categorical feature lets it learn these persistent effects directly, beyond the E009 behavioral/demographic features.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full 371-feature table: added a single categorical feature 'hh' = household_key (2,498 categories). All other features unchanged.
reasoning_summary: The target is household-persistent (per-household median of past targets alone beats the global median by 40% in a proxy check), and all validation households overlap train households, so identity is learnable — but no existing feature encodes it.

hypothesis: Precomputed point predictors — decay-weighted averages of target-aligned 28-day windows (the exact target horizon shifted back), tenure-aware renormalized variants, and window-shape statistics — give the model near-sufficient statistics of the strongest signal, so it can calibrate them (tenure truncation, snapshot-level bias) instead of rediscovering them from 368 raw columns.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full 368-feature table: added 20 features — decay-weighted averages of the 13 target-aligned 28-day windows (spend_28, tlag_2..tlag_13) at decay 0.5/0.6/0.65/0.7/0.8, tenure-aware renormalized versions of each, log1p, median/trimmed mean, trend slope, CV, max, leading-zero streak, momentum ratio, activity share, tenure-aware mean.
reasoning_summary: A no-fit decay-weighted window average alone reaches MAE ~62.9 on a strict time-aware proxy, matching the full fitted model — so feeding these sufficient statistics (plus tenure-aware variants that fix early-snapshot truncation bias) should let the model calibrate them and break the 62.3 plateau.

hypothesis: Churn/hazard and seasonality predict future spend: the share of zero-spend stride-7 28-day windows, weekly-mean spend in those windows, its coefficient of variation, and household/global seasonal profiles of the next 4 weeks add signal beyond E009's level, trend and lag features.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full table: added 7 features — zero-rate, mean and CV of spend across up to 12 stride-7 aligned 28-day windows, household seasonal profile (next-4-weeks relative spend, ×weekly mean), global next-4-weeks seasonality, and due_ratio (days since last trip / mean inter-trip gap).
reasoning_summary: Stride-7 aligned windows measure the household's own 4-week-ahead rhythm (zero-rate correlates −0.39 with future spend) and seasonal profiles capture next-month demand; both are computable for train and validation snapshots alike, avoiding the year-ago distribution shift that hurt E010/E013/E014.

hypothesis: Category-level purchase-cycle timing predicts future spend: for each commodity a household buys on a repeat basis, its next purchase is due roughly one inter-visit-gap after the last visit; summing mean spend over commodities due within the next 28 days (gap capped at 30/60/90) yields a spend projection that captures WHEN dollars will arrive, not just how much was recently spent.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full 371-feature table: added 13 category-cycle features — projected next-28d spend from per-commodity inter-visit gaps (clipped 30/60/90), #due categories, #active categories, gap-pressure sums, EWMA-weighted projection, and per-active normalizations.
reasoning_summary: Target-aligned lags average over the same phase of past cycles; the cycle projection instead predicts the next cycle directly from inter-purchase timing, adding phase information the lag averages lack. Partial correlation with spend_28 (~0.32) suggests incremental signal.

hypothesis: A pruned, noise-reduced feature set beats the full E009 pool: the E011 table plus only the 24 genuinely new extras from the hazard/seasonality (zrate_7s, wmean_7s, wcv_7s, due_ratio) and decayed-predictor (dec50..dec80, med13, trim13, slope13, cv13, max13, zero_streak, momentum, act13) branches, with dead/leaky columns (row-order index, whitespace dept cols, tlag_16..18) excluded.
transformation_description: Rebuilt table as e011_pruned (352 clean cols) + 24 new extras from E016/E017 branches; no other changes.
reasoning_summary: E011 (pruned) already matched E009; adding only the strongest survivors from the hazard and decay branches may add signal without the noise that hurt E013–E018.

hypothesis: The E009 feature pool is over-shrunk by the harness's fixed L2 penalty: uniformly scaling all numeric features down to 0.3× of their standardized magnitude emulates ~11x stronger ridge regularization, reducing coefficient noise and improving validation MAE. If the harness's model is scale-invariant (standardizes internally), the result is identical to E009 and nothing is lost.
transformation_description: On top of E009's full 371-feature table: multiplied all 364 numeric feature columns by 0.3 (categorical/bool columns untouched); no features added or removed.
reasoning_summary: Offline ridge experiments showed large lambda sensitivity: emulating ~11x stronger L2 (via 0.3x feature scaling) improved internal temporal-split MAE from 64.20 to 63.50, suggesting the fixed harness model is under-regularized for this 369-feature pool; scaling down features is the only way to increase effective regularization without changing the harness, and is a no-op if the harness standardizes.
